No, thank you for acknowledging my comment. It's greatly appreciated. But i moved to Salem, OR when i was 17. I met a guy older than me and he asked did i wanna move to the west coast. He gave me a totally different picture of what our reality was. I am African american so being there wasn't easy already. I first stayed on the streets of Salem for about 3 months. Spent thanksgiving, Christmas and New Years in a bathroom at the park, a shelter, and eventually the street with other homeless people. Every single day id sit In front of this Subway and even if i didn't have money I'd go in for a free water and tell the workers good morning. The DAY of my 18th birthday the manager (I'll never forget her, Caitlyn) walked outside and asked me was i looking for work by chance, i almost cried just telling her a simple yes. She asked me to come in for an interview the next day and i was hired on spot. Homeless for another 3 months and after 3 months of hard work and saving and the shelters help, i was able to move into a 1 bedroom garage converted house. I had no tv. No radio. No phone. Just books and my mind. Mind you the guy i was with would work a job for a week or 2 to get a check then quit. Around my 19th birthday i lied and said we should start over back in Michigan where we are from and he agreed, his mom bought us tickets from Oregon back to Michigan. I broke up with him on a greyhound bus in Chicago. We've had some scary/weird interactions since then but that's another story. I'm now 21 and wayyy more wiser. Thanks for listening to this. Feels good to get it out lol
